The skeleton on the right is a bipedal theropod (likely a Tyrannosaurus or similar). A human visitor stands in the foreground for scale, looking up at the exhibits. The lighting is dim with spotlights on the fossils.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The Triceratops skull on the left clearly displays the iconic three-horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a skeletal mount where the post-cranial body is largely obscured or incomplete; the focus is on the skull. checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, solid bony frill is the most dominant feature of the skull on the left, extending significantly backward.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) and shows the characteristic rough texture and marginal ossifications (epoccipitals) along the edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject is a fossilized skeleton; no skin, scales, or soft tissue are present to evaluate.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The full body posture and comparative limb lengths are not clearly visible due to the angle and the fact that it is a partial skeletal mount.
